## Highlights

**A secret written as a shell default is now reported.** `token=${SOME_VAR:-<value>}` used to pass as a plain variable reference, so a real credential supplied as the fallback was never found. An opaque operand of `:-`, `:=`, `:+` or `:?` now counts as the value, and only the operand is reported and masked: `token=${SOME_VAR:-[REDACTED]}`.

## Upgrade notes

No configuration changes.

New findings can appear on lines with a shell default that holds an opaque value. Each one is a value your shell really uses when the variable is unset (or, for `:+`, when it is set), so check it before allowlisting it. A `[[allowlist.rules]]` regex for such a value now matches the operand, not the whole expansion.

Upgrade: `brew upgrade vshuraeff/tap/sekretbarilo`, then `sekretbarilo doctor`.

## Changes

### Detection

- A whole `${NAME:-value}`, `${NAME:=value}`, `${NAME:+value}` or `${NAME:?value}` is judged by its operand under every rule except `password-in-url`, which keeps its own reference check. Stopwords, allowlists, the password strength check and the entropy gate see the operand alone, so a word in the variable's name no longer hides the value. A hash word in the name (`COMMIT_SHA`) still reads a hex operand as a digest, as it does a bare hex value.
- The expansion stays a reference when the operand is empty, holds whitespace, is a path, reads as code or words (`changeme`, `$OTHER`, `$(cat /run/secrets/key)`), or, under an entropy-gated rule, is shorter than 16 bytes.

### Known limits

- The unquoted form of `generic-password-assignment` stops at a brace, so `PASSWORD=${NAME:-<value>}` is still not read. The quoted form is.
- An operand in its own quotes (`token="${NAME:-"<value>"}"`, `${NAME:-'<value>'}`) is still not read.
- A password default whose pieces read as short words stays a reference, even when the same value alone would be reported.
- An operand that reads as a path stays a reference, so a short opaque directory inside it (`${NAME:-/tmp/<value>/state.lock}`) is not reported, as in earlier versions.
